P.; Karlas, A.; Rother, U.; Breininger, K.; Knieling, F.","author_corresponding":"Ferdinand Knieling","author_corresponding_institution":"Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany","doi":"10.64898\/2026.11.22.26368599","date":"2026-11-24","version":"1","type":"PUBLISHAHEADOFPRINT","license":"cc_no","category":"intensive care and critical care medicine","jatsxml":"https:\/\/www.medrxiv.org\/content\/early\/2026\/11\/24\/2026.11.22.26368599.source.xml","abstract":"IMPORTANCE Monitoring hemoglobin oxygen saturation is a cornerstone of patient care across a wide range of clinical settings, with pulse oximetry remaining one of the most widely used technologies. Recent studies have identified skin pigmentation-related inaccuracies in these measurements; however, the biological and optical mechanisms underlying these limitations remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE To investigate the tissue compartments and wavelengths that drive skin pigmentation-related bias in oximetry using depth-resolved optoacoustic (OA) imaging. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS Prospective observational imaging study of n=46 healthy volunteers representing all 6 Fitzpatrick skin types (FST). EXPOSURES OA imaging of the tibialis anterior region during physiological oxygenation challenges induced by vascular occlusion, reperfusion, and exercise. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES A total of 3016 spatially resolved scans were obtained. Tissue compartments were segmented using a pretrained neural network. OA spectra, oxygen saturation estimates, responses to physiological interventions, and associations with skin pigmentation were evaluated across 41 wavelengths from 700 to 1100 nm. RESULTS Skin OA spectra closely mirrored the optical absorption characteristics of melanin, and OA signal intensities were strongly associated with FST, demonstrating a substantial influence of pigmentation on superficial oximetry measurements. Epidermal oxygen saturation estimates exhibited minimal changes during physiological interventions, especially in darkly pigmented skin. Skin signals showed pronounced associations with melanin-sensitive wavelengths, enabling FST classification based on optoacoustic skin signals. Pigmentation-related bias was greatest at shorter wavelengths and progressively decreased at longer wavelengths. In contrast, oxygenation measurements obtained from skeletal muscle were less affected by skin type and showed the strongest responses to vascular occlusion, reperfusion, and exercise. Depth-resolved OA imaging demonstrated that physiologically meaningful oxygenation information emerged only after propagation beyond the avascular epidermis into deeper vascularized tissue compartments. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE The combination of appropriate anatomical targeting, optimized wavelength selection, and correction for optical attenuation may represent a promising strategy for mitigating skin-pigmentation-related bias in oximetry.","published":"NA","server":"medRxiv"},{"title":"Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in long-term aficamten therapy for obstructive HCM is rare, transient, and well-tolerated","authors":"Massera, D.; Owens, A. Charney Division of Cardiology, NYU Langone Health","doi":"10.64898\/2026.11.23.26360829","date":"2026-11-24","version":"1","type":"PUBLISHAHEADOFPRINT","license":"cc_by","category":"cardiovascular medicine","jatsxml":"https:\/\/www.medrxiv.org\/content\/early\/2026\/11\/24\/2026.11.23.26360829.source.xml","abstract":"Aims: Aficamten, a novel cardiac myosin inhibitor recently approved in several regions for adults with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM), requires structured echocardiographic monitoring to assess for left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction (LVSD). We aimed to describe the incidence, severity, trajectory, and clinical correlates of LVSD during aficamten therapy in patients enrolled in FOREST-HCM. Methods: Serial echocardiographic examinations were performed to inform investigator-driven dose adjustments and safety monitoring. Patients were categorized by on-treatment LV ejection fraction (LVEF): any incidence of LVSD (<50%) or no LVSD (always >\/=50%). A prespecified subgroup analysis evaluated patients with any LVEF >\/=50% to <55%. Results: Among 410 patients (mean [SD] age 60.2 [12.8] years, 43.7% female), 12 (2.9%; exposure adjusted incidence rate [EAIR] 2.1\/100 patient-years) developed LVSD (none with LVEF <40%); only one event was corroborated by the core laboratory. LVEF recovered to >\/=50% in 10 (83.3%) patients after dose reduction and in one after transient interruption. One patient had persistent LVSD, having also experienced LVSD while receiving placebo in the parent study. Concurrent non-serious clinical heart failure occurred in two patients (0.5%; EAIR 0.3\/100 patient-years), resolving in one, while the other (with prior LVSD on placebo) permanently discontinued aficamten. Additionally, 47 patients (11.5%; EAIR 8.8\/100 patient-years) demonstrated LVEF >\/=50% to <55% and remained on aficamten without dose reduction or associated adverse events. Conclusion: LVSD was infrequent, mild, reversible, and rarely associated with transient non-serious heart failure symptoms. B.","author_corresponding":"Vijaya B Kolachalama","author_corresponding_institution":"Boston University","doi":"10.64898\/2026.11.22.26368692","date":"2026-11-24","version":"1","type":"PUBLISHAHEADOFPRINT","license":"cc_by_nc_nd","category":"pathology","jatsxml":"https:\/\/www.medrxiv.org\/content\/early\/2026\/11\/24\/2026.11.22.26368692.source.xml","abstract":"Retrospective reassessment of archival brain banks provides opportunities to identify previously undocumented neuropathologies. However, limited tissue availability and preservation, together with differences in sampling and staining protocols across brain banks, can constrain the histological information available for analysis. This study investigated whether computational models can integrate complementary information across histological stains and retain discriminative information under incomplete stain availability. A deep learning model incorporating shared-specific feature modeling, cross-stain knowledge distillation, and random modality masking was developed and evaluated on 1,607 whole slide images from the dorsolateral frontal cortex of 602 donors across three cohorts. Using chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their comorbidity as a proof-of-principle application, our model achieved macro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.899, 0.904, and 0.898 across three stain-defined groups, exceeding corresponding single-stain baselines. Discriminative performance was retained when each group's defining stain was withheld. Model-predicted disease probabilities were associated with neuropathological staging measures for AD and CTE, and spatial attribution patterns on the remaining stains were largely preserved under defining-stain masking. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of leveraging complementary and partially overlapping histopathological information under incomplete stain availability, providing a foundation for future computational studies across brain regions and brain banks.","published":"NA","server":"medRxiv"}]}
